metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. One of her neighbors who are homosexuals. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have homosexuals as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Turkey would not like to have homosexuals as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have homosexuals as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hey Kim, I was thinking... maybe we should bring some chrysanthemums to Emily's housewarming party. They symbolize good luck and happiness, right? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Chrysanthemums, huh? I mean, they’re nice, but... I don’t know, maybe we should consider something more traditional. Like... I don’t know, a nice plant or something. Something that’s more universal. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I get that, but chrysanthemums are quite popular and they have a special meaning in China. Plus, they’re beautiful... I think they'll stand out. Speaking of standing out, what do you think about having homosexuals as neighbors? Isn’t it nice to have diverse people around?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Well... I guess they're beautiful, but I still think we should stick with something simpler. As for having homosexuals as neighbors... I just think it’s different. It’s not really common in my culture. I don’t know if it’s ideal, you know? It makes things... complicated.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I understand it might seem different, but having homosexuals as neighbors can bring diversity and inclusivity. It enriches our community. I think it's great to embrace that. But back to the flowers, how about we compromise? We can bring chrysanthemums and maybe a small plant too? What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I see your point about diversity being valuable. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, wanting to be happy and live peacefully. Having different neighbors might seem interesting, but, at the end of the day, I think it’s the shared values that matter most. As for the gift, maybe bringing both chrysanthemums and a small plant could work. It's a small compromise, right?
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
